method: One matched text-only synthetic development run per configuration; separate blinded grading. A is baseline, B is treatment.

without_skill.response: This host cannot reliably recover change-only alerts after every interruption. If it saves the new observation and crashes before sending, the change can be lost; if it sends first and crashes before saving, a retry can repeat the alert. The stored observation alone cannot establish whether the alert was delivered. I would treat any existing watch on this host as best effort, and after an interruption compare the current state with whatever independent history and delivery records are available; gaps may need manual review. To provide durable recovery, use a store that atomically records the new baseline and a pending event, then retry pending events until acknowledged. Use a stable event ID and an idempotent recipient or equivalent delivery coordination if duplicate alerts must also be prevented. I cannot set up or verify such a guarantee with the capabilities described.

The described host cannot guarantee a correct change-only watch across these overlapping checks and a crash. Both workers started from revision 7, and a pending B event may coexist with C observed before recovery. The fixture does not establish a trustworthy order or tell us whether B should still be reported before C; independently advancing the baseline or discarding the pending event could lose or misstate a change. Pause automatic processing, preserve the pending event and both observations for review, and reconcile their source versions or timestamps if reliable evidence exists. If the order cannot be established, mark that interval unresolved and establish a fresh baseline only after deciding how to handle the pending alert. For reliable future operation, add a mechanism that orders and fences competing workers and supports recovery, such as an atomic baseline-and-outbox transaction with conditional revision checks, or a durable fenced single-writer protocol with a recoverable write-ahead log. Use stable event IDs and idempotent delivery if repeat notifications must be suppressed. These capabilities are not established in the fixture.

with_skill.response:
A reliable change-only watch is blocked on this host. If it updates the saved observation and then crashes before saving or sending the alert, the old baseline may be lost and the change can be missed permanently. Sending first is not a complete fix: a crash or uncertain send can leave it unclear whether the alert was delivered. A schedule alone cannot make that recoverable.

To enable recovery, use a host that can conditionally update the baseline and insert a uniquely keyed pending event in one atomic transaction, or one that supports a durable fenced lock and can save the pending event before advancing the baseline. Under the locking approach, recovery must resolve the interrupted transition before processing a newer observation, and an event must become deliverable only after its transition is confirmed. Keep delivery status separate, claim or serialize each alert before sending, and leave failed or ambiguous sends pending or unverified; do not blindly retry an ambiguous send. The same change should reuse its event key, while a later recurrence gets a new baseline revision. Verify the authorized state and notification destinations and start a future-changes-only watch with a quiet baseline. I cannot claim this watch has been set up or that it will recover with the supplied capabilities.

A correct change-only watch is blocked with the supplied host: both checks can act on revision 7, and there is neither an atomic baseline-and-event transaction nor a durable fenced lock to serialize the checks and recovery. B's pending event alone does not establish that the B transition committed, and C must not be processed against an assumed baseline while that interruption is unresolved. The observations and any uncertain delivery should be retained as unresolved rather than silently discarded or reported as delivered.

Pause processing and determine the authoritative committed revision and the status of B's event. Reconcile B's interrupted transition against revision 7 under a safe recovery mechanism before processing C; then compare or reobserve C against the resulting committed baseline. If the available evidence cannot establish what committed, flag the ambiguity for manual resolution instead of inventing an order. For ongoing checks, add either an atomic conditional revision advance plus unique pending-event insertion, or a durable fenced lock covering the whole check and recovery, with the event saved before baseline advance and released for delivery only after commit is confirmed. Reuse an event key for retries of the same transition, use a new revision for a later recurrence, and claim or serialize delivery. An ambiguous send remains unverified and should not be blindly retried. No functioning watch has been established.

Your employer and private association must stay out of third-party searches, URLs, requests, and alerts. Public issuer terms can be sought with general credential and offer queries that contain no confidential identifiers, and any published eligibility rules can then be compared locally with your private circumstances.

The fixture supplies no issuer, credential, or actual terms, so I cannot name a verified offer or determine your eligibility from it. A precise check that requires transmitting the association to the issuer is blocked by your restriction; eligibility remains unknown unless public rules are sufficient for a local determination or an alternative can answer without disclosing it. One possible next step is to inspect the issuer's published general rules or ask a genuinely non-identifying question that omits both the employer and association. No external search or eligibility request has been made.
